11811.d: Kompositsioon viie naise ja kuue lapsega. Valges ruumis tumerohelisel diivanil istuvad: šotiruudulise vestiga poiss, tema kõrval sinistes teksades heleda pluusiga naine, kelle käsi toetub diivani käsitoele. Tema kõrval istuval naisel on süles väike kirjus kleidis tüdruk. Paremal istub kahe pika patsiga pidulikult riides tütarlaps. Diivani taga seisavad kolm naist - igal neist väike laps süles.
11811.de: A composition with five women and six children. In a white room, sitting on a dark green sofa: a boy in a tartan waistcoat, beside him a woman in blue jeans and a light blouse, whose hand rests on the armrest of the sofa. The woman sitting beside her has on her lap a small girl in a patterned dress. On the right sits a girl with two long braids, dressed festively. Behind the sofa stand three women - each with a small child in her arms.

11812.d: Viis rahvarõivais naist Tallinna lauluväljaku taustal. Pilti ääristab rahvariidevööd kujutav raamistik. Alaosas vööga ümbritsetud ristkülikus kiri "Tallinn". Pildi üldtonaalsus punakas-oranžikas, vöökiri punase, musta, kollasega. Üldmuljelt 1980ndate laulupeo plakateid meenutav.
11812.de: Five women in folk costumes against the background of the Tallinn Song Festival Grounds. The picture is bordered by a frame depicting a folk costume belt. In the lower part, within a rectangle surrounded by a belt, the inscription "Tallinn". The overall tonality of the picture is reddish-orange, the belt inscription in red, black, yellow. Generally reminiscent of song festival posters of the 1980s.

11813.d: Heledas, vanaaegses interjööris istuvad viis lillelistes kleitides naist kohvilaua taga. Laud kaetud kuuele. Serviis peenemustriline, kohvikann valge. Laual jalaga vaagen, millel kook. Klaasvaasis tume roos. Foto imiteerib 1930ndate meeleolu. Paspartuu hallikast papist, ümarnurkse avaga. Mustal raamil kullatud siseserv, millel kärbsemusta jälgi.
11813.de: Five women in floral dresses sit at a coffee table in a bright, old-fashioned interior. Table set for six. Finely patterned service, white coffee pot. On the table a footed dish with a cake. A dark rose in a glass vase. The photo imitates the mood of the 1930s. Mount of grayish cardboard, with a rounded-corner opening. Gilded inner edge on the black frame, with traces of fly dirt.

11814.d: Viis hommikumantlis naist paneelmaja köögis. Paremal kandiline laud, millel teekann, mõned tassid, lilled jm. esemed. Aknast paistab hall paneelmaja. Kolmel naisel on käes tass, kaks on kummardunud lugemismaterjali kohale.
11814.de: Five women in dressing gowns in the kitchen of a panel building. On the right a square table, on which a teapot, a few cups, flowers and other objects. Through the window a grey panel building can be seen. Three of the women hold a cup, two are bent over reading material.

In the foreground of the photo five young women stand in a row, wearing soldier's clothing, dark laced boots on their feet. All stand with legs apart, hands behind their backs. Their faces are striped with camouflage paint. In the background a large blackening round opening.

11816.d: Öises miljöös viis nahkriietes noort naist tumeda Fordi ees. Esiplaanil kükakil kaks tugevasti meigitud naist. Keskel auto ees seisab punakate juustega naine, käed värvlil. Tagapool, auto kapotil istuvad kaks naist, vasakpoolsel seljas lühike seelik. Teistel pikad mustad püskid jalas. Iga naise juurde kirjutatud hõbedase markeriga nimi.
11816.de: In a night setting, five young women in leather clothing in front of a dark Ford. In the foreground two heavily made-up women crouch. In the middle, in front of the car, stands a woman with reddish hair, hands on the fender. Further back, sitting on the car's bonnet, two women, the one on the left wearing a short skirt. The others wear long black trousers. Each woman's name is written next to her in silver marker.

11817.d: Naeratava noore naise portreefoto. Juuksed punakasblondid, kaela ümber tumeroheline sall, taust helesinine. Helikassetil naishääl leob mina-vormis horoskoobilaadset teksti.

11841.d: Kolmeosaline fotomontaaž moodustab ühtse tervikliku kujundi lamavast mehest pealtvaates. Mehe käed on tõstetud üles, küünarnukkidest kõverdatud. Pea pöördes vasaku õla suunas, silmad suletud. Kasutatud mosaiikseid, ristkülikulaadseid motiive. Kasutatud ka mängukaardimotiivi. Kujutis on must-valge. II ja III osa kergelt koloreeritud punakates-sinistes toonides. III osal sama motiiv, mis I osal, ent tunduvalt tihedam ja suurem.
11841.de: A three-part photomontage forms a unified overall image of a reclining man seen from above. The man's arms are raised, bent at the elbows. The head turned towards the left shoulder, eyes closed. Mosaic-like, rectangular motifs are used. A playing-card motif is also used. The image is black-and-white. Parts II and III are lightly coloured in reddish-blue tones. Part III has the same motif as Part I, but considerably denser and larger.

11842.d: Fotokollaaž tükkideks lõigatud ja veidi nihestatult kokku pandud ansambel Röövel Ööbiku liikmete (Tõnu Pedaru, Tarvo Hanno Varres, Raul Saaremets, Allan Hmelintski) fotoportreedest. Must-valgete fotoportreede fragmentide vahel trükitud kujutised linnumotiividega joonistustest, fotodest, mosaiikidest ja maalidest.
11842.de: Photo collage of an ensemble cut into pieces and assembled somewhat displaced, of photo portraits of the members of the band Röövel Ööbik (Tõnu Pedaru, Tarvo Hanno Varres, Raul Saaremets, Allan Hmelintski). Between the fragments of black-and-white photo portraits printed images with bird motifs from drawings, photos, mosaics and paintings.

11843.d: Kuuest paneelist koosnev fotokollaaž, mida eksponeeritakse tervikuna. Kujutis koosneb värvilistest ja must-valgetest fotofragmentidest, millel on kujutatud erinevaid naisenägusid (teiste seas Ly Unt, Ene-Liis Semper) näo- ja kehaosi, kumminuku detaile, rindade mulaaži, triipkoodi. All paremal servas ulatub kujutise serv (naise puus) pildiraamist väljapoole. Fotopaneeli keskosas ripub raamitud hologrammkujutis - heledapäise naise portree (Maria Avdjuško).
11843.de: A photo collage consisting of six panels, exhibited as a whole. The image consists of colour and black-and-white photo fragments depicting various women's faces (among others Ly Unt, Ene-Liis Semper), face and body parts, details of a rubber doll, a breast mould, a barcode. In the lower right corner, the edge of the image (a woman's hip) extends beyond the picture frame. In the centre of the photo panel hangs a framed hologram image - a portrait of a fair-haired woman (Maria Avdjuško).

11844.d: "Sugar Free" on autori hullumajakogemusel põhinev installatsioon, milles on kesksel kohal metallvardaga ühendatud poolringis liikuv antiikne puidust kapp. Seinal on 18 fotofragmendist koosnev kujutis hoonest. Selle kõrval fotod autorist, millede all sildid "After" ja "Before". Kapi sisemuses on metalltrossidega rippuma kinnitatud tükksuhkruga täidetud metallist linnupuur, mille kohal põleb kaabli otsas rippuv elektripirn. Kapist kõlab helitaust (esimeses versioonis autor lugemas põhiseaduse paragrahve, teises versioonis katkend Gibson Brothersi palast "Paranoia").
11844.de: "Sugar Free" is an installation based on the author's experience of a madhouse, in which the central place is occupied by an antique wooden cabinet moving in a semicircle connected by a metal rod. On the wall is an 18-photo-fragment image of a building. Next to it are photos of the author, under which are signs "After" and "Before". Inside the cabinet, a metal birdcage filled with sugar cubes is suspended on metal cables, above which burns an electric light bulb hanging on a cable. A soundtrack sounds from the cabinet (in the first version the author reading paragraphs of the Constitution, in the second version an excerpt from the Gibson Brothers' song "Paranoia").

11845.d: Videoinstallatsioon kahest kõrvuti asetsevast videoprojektsioonist, milledest ühel kujutatud alasti lamavat naist, kelle kehal lebavad kutsikad. Teisel videol kujutatud keskmise suurusega koera. Helitaustaks koera niutsumine.
11845.de: Video installation of two side-by-side video projections, one of which depicts a nude woman lying down, with puppies lying on her body. The other video depicts a medium-sized dog. Sound background of a dog whimpering.

12025.d: Tavapärasel poeriiulil seisavad rivis kümned erinevad massitoote kaubad. Teose kontseptuaalne nihestatus seisneb selles, et kunstnik on pakenditel ära vahetanud tarbijale tuttavad kaubamärgid: näiteks leidub riiulil Marlboro šampoon, Snickersi kalakonserv, Pedigree cornflakes, Omo müsli, Ariel limonaad, Nokia Coca-Cola, Coca-Cola ketšup jne.
12025.de: On a regular store shelf stand dozens of different mass-product goods in rows. The conceptual displacement of the work lies in the fact that the artist has swapped the brand names familiar to the consumer on the packaging: for example, the shelf includes Marlboro shampoo, Snickers canned fish, Pedigree cornflakes, Omo muesli, Ariel lemonade, Nokia Coca-Cola, Coca-Cola ketchup, etc.

12028.d: Eetriaktsioon "Kodumaa uudised" oli Kanal 2 programmis 27., 28. ja 29. septembril 1996. Päevauudiste põhjal luuakse poeetilised tekstid-luuletused, riimitud banaalsuses. Uudised kajastavad Eestis toimuvaid majandus-, poliitika- ja kultuurisündmusi. Võõristusvahendiks on esitatava riimitus. Seda loevad näitlejad, parem kui naine ja mees korraga kaadris. Neid on eelnevalt instrueeritud. Protsess on viimistletud ja lavastatud. Tulemust esitatakse kolmel erineval päeval Kanal 2 kaudu vahetult enne ametlikke uudiseid. Kogupikkus poolteist kuni kolm minutit.
12028.de: The broadcast action "Kodumaa uudised" ["National News"] was on Kanal 2's programme on 27, 28 and 29 September 1996. Based on the daily news, poetic texts-poems are created, rhymed banality. The news covers economic, political and cultural events taking place in Estonia. The alienation device is the lack of rhyme in the delivery. It is read by actors, preferably a woman and a man in the frame at the same time. They have been instructed beforehand. The process is polished and staged. The result is presented on three different days via Kanal 2 immediately before the official news. Total length one and a half to three minutes.

47503.d: Estonia as a country first participated in the Venice Biennale in 1997. The artists were chosen by a special committee at the Cultural Endowment of Estonia and not through an open competition as became the rule after 1999 when CCA took over. In 1997, Estonia was represented by Jaan Toomik, Raoul Kurvitz and Siim-Tanel Annus who held performances on the waterfront near San Marco. 47506.d: The Estonian Pavilion at the 48th Venice biennale included two art projects: one by artists Peeter Pere and Jüri Ojaver (curated by Johannes Saar ) and the other a solo project by artist Ando Keskküla. Both exhibitions were located at Palazzo Querini. Curator Johannes Saar: “Estonia is represented on the Venice Biennial by three middle aged, married man again. It might happen to be a embarrassing problem in the galaxy of Political Correctness, but people in Estonia don’t worry about that yet. On the contrary, in the bigger frame of Venice Biennial we are forgiven in advance as newcomers who may turn out to be a source of new blood. It would be extremely short-sighted to enter the Big Picture under the slogan of male art anyway. The curiosity called “man” has been reduced in contemporary art to a much more marginal appearance like that of Estonia on the edge of a unifying Europe. A locational similarity that gives us direction to carry on with the subject. We are redrawing the map of European culture in “reborn Estonia” at the moment and this kind of world conquest is traditionally blamed on men. Any kind of challenging statement is. Nevertheless, no matter how deeply a modernistic

47549.d:
Photo series “Grandfather” is based on the story of a little girl, who after the death of her grandfather scratched out his face from the family photos; because her grandfather had died and did not exist any more. Children’s hands don’t understand that photography is the memory’s aide and history’s tool – they just carry out the grandfather’s death on the photos. As Peeter Linnap said in the catalogue for the 2nd Saaremaa Biennial titled Invasion (where this work was first exhibited), “the artist does not start to decompose these specific pictures, as much as the general myth of photos as a prostehtic of reality.” These photos leave us alone with a cultural agreement and the spirits of time.

Media: “Another very interesting exhibit is from Mari Laanemetsa – a photo series Grandfather (1997) which is based on the story of a girl who after the death of her grandfather scratched his face out of her photos. Also in Laanemetsa’s vintage group pictures, which show people in different situations, there is one participant without a face. The result is an amazingly expressive and gives an idea of ​​both the power and limits of fotomedia. ”
